papers.title: What can we learn about Reionization astrophysical parameters using Gaussian Process Regression?
papers.abstract: Reionization is one of the least understood processes in the evolution history of the Universe, mostly because of the numerous astrophysical processes occurring simultaneously about which we do not have a very clear idea so far. In this article, we use the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) method to learn the reionization history and infer the astrophysical parameters. We reconstruct the UV luminosity density function using the HFF and early JWST data. From the reconstructed history of reionization, the global differential brightness temperature fluctuation during this epoch has been computed. We perform MCMC analysis of the global 21-cm signal using the instrumental specifications of SARAS, in combination with Lyman-$α$ ionization fraction data, Planck optical depth measurements and UV luminosity data. Our analysis reveals that GPR can help infer the astrophysical parameters in a model-agnostic way than conventional methods. Additionally, we analyze the 21-cm power spectrum using the reconstructed history of reionization and demonstrate how the future 21-cm mission SKA, in combination with Planck and Lyman-$α$ forest data, improves the bounds on the reionization astrophysical parameters by doing a joint MCMC analysis for the astrophysical parameters plus 6 cosmological parameters for $Λ$CDM model. The results make the GPR-based reconstruction technique a robust learning process and the inferences on the astrophysical parameters obtained therefrom are quite reliable that can be used for future analysis.

llm.why_not_core: This paper uses Gaussian Process Regression for astrophysical reionization inference, with no connection to FEA, surrogate modeling for structural mechanics, or biomedical implant design.

summary_en.motivation: To infer astrophysical parameters of reionization in a model-agnostic manner using Gaussian Process Regression.

summary_en.result: GPR-based reconstruction yields reliable parameter inferences, and joint analysis with future SKA data tightens constraints on astrophysical parameters.
summary_en.validation: Validation using observational data from HFF, early JWST, Planck, and Lyman-α forest.

papers.title: Improved physics-informed neural network in mitigating gradient related failures
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate fundamental physical principles with advanced data-driven techniques, driving significant advancements in scientific computing. However, PINNs face persistent challenges with stiffness in gradient flow, which limits their predictive capabilities. This paper presents an improved PINN (I-PINN) to mitigate gradient-related failures. The core of I-PINN is to combine the respective strengths of neural networks with an improved architecture and adaptive weights containingupper bounds. The capability to enhance accuracy by at least one order of magnitude and accelerate convergence, without introducing extra computational complexity relative to the baseline model, is achieved by I-PINN. Numerical experiments with a variety of benchmarks illustrate the improved accuracy and generalization of I-PINN. The supporting data and code are accessible at https://github.com/PanChengN/I-PINN.git, enabling broader research engagement.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or any implant/biomechanics application, and only validates on standard PDE benchmarks.

summary_en.motivation: To overcome gradient-related failures in physics-informed neural networks that degrade predictive accuracy and convergence.
summary_en.method: An improved PINN architecture is proposed that combines network enhancements with adaptive upper-bound weights.
summary_en.result: The method achieves at least one order of magnitude accuracy improvement and faster convergence without extra computational cost.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on a variety of standard PDE benchmark problems.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Data Shapley via Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: As data plays an increasingly pivotal role in decision-making, the emergence of data markets underscores the growing importance of data valuation. Within the machine learning landscape, Data Shapley stands out as a widely embraced method for data valuation. However, a limitation of Data Shapley is its assumption of a fixed dataset, contrasting with the dynamic nature of real-world applications where data constantly evolves and expands. This paper establishes the relationship between Data Shapley and infinite-order U-statistics and addresses this limitation by quantifying the uncertainty of Data Shapley with changes in data distribution from the perspective of U-statistics. We make statistical inferences on data valuation to obtain confidence intervals for the estimations. We construct two different algorithms to estimate this uncertainty and provide recommendations for their applicable situations. We also conduct a series of experiments on various datasets to verify asymptotic normality and propose a practical trading scenario enabled by this method.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address expensive simulation sampling, surrogate modeling, constraint handling, or any biomedical/implant design application.

summary_en.motivation: Data Shapley assumes a fixed dataset, but real-world data evolves; this work quantifies uncertainty due to distribution changes.
summary_en.method: Establishes a connection between Data Shapley and infinite-order U-statistics to derive confidence intervals via statistical inference.
summary_en.result: Constructs two algorithms for uncertainty estimation and demonstrates asymptotic normality on multiple datasets.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation on various datasets to verify theoretical properties and a practical trading scenario.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文比较了不同股骨柄对骨重塑的影响，直接关联到髋关节植入物的应力遮挡评估，但缺乏接触力学和微动分析。

summary_en.motivation: To compare femoral bone remodeling patterns between two cementless stem designs after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Clinical follow-up with radiographic evaluation of bone mineral density changes in Gruen zones.
summary_en.result: Different bone remodeling patterns were observed between the short-tapered wedge stem and fully HA-coated stem.
summary_en.validation: Validated using patient cohort data with DXA or radiographic analysis.
